info.title: Life Links Application HTTP API
info.description: Published v1 contract for the implemented Life Links application HTTP surface. It covers the web and native application workflows plus the stable QR browser entry point. Runtime health, readiness, version, and generic SPA fallback routes are operational or implementation details and are intentionally outside this contract.

post.summary: Create a browser-cookie or native-bearer session
post.description: Browser callers omit `client` and receive an HTTP-only session cookie. Native callers send `client: native` and receive `sessionToken`. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; the native login envelope may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Delete the active session when present
post.description: The operation is idempotent and succeeds even when no valid session exists. It clears the browser session cookie and deletes the authenticated bearer or cookie session when present. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: List links owned by the authenticated user

patch.description: Only the authenticated owner can update a link. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Upload one image or video to an owned link
post.description: The multipart field name is `file`. One file of at most 25 MiB is accepted, with at most eight media records per link. Supported MIME types are image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, and video/quicktime. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Read public media or owner-authorized private media

delete.summary: Delete media from an owned link
delete.description: Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: List top-level Life Links or one owned Life Link's immediate children
get.description: Omit `parentId` to list top-level Life Links. Supply an owned `parentId` to list only its immediate children. Results sort by normalized title, creation time, then stable ID and page with an opaque cursor; the endpoint never recursively returns the whole hierarchy.

post.summary: Create a private top-level or child Life Link
post.description: Creates one Life Link with title, body, structured-body, and privacy defaults when omitted. An optional parent must belong to the authenticated owner. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Search the authenticated owner's Life Links
get.description: Performs bounded, owner-scoped search across title, compatibility body text, recorded ancestor path, and QR identity. Match classes rank exact QR, exact or prefix title, title, recorded path, then body; results within a class sort by normalized title, updatedAt descending, then stable ID. Each result includes bounded path and body context plus explicit truncation and continuation metadata.

get.summary: Read one owned Life Link with bounded hierarchy context
get.description: Returns the exact canonical Life Link, a bounded ancestry path, and a bounded page of immediate children. Truncation and continuation metadata is explicit; no public QR response exposes this hierarchy.

patch.summary: Update one owned Life Link's content or privacy
patch.description: Requires the exact `expectedUpdatedAt` revision returned by a prior owner read. Stale writes fail with `409 stale_life_link`; the server never silently overwrites a newer human or agent draft. Parent placement and QR binding are not accepted here. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

patch.summary: Replace one owned Life Link's parent or detach it to the top level
patch.description: Set `parentId` to an owned Life Link or null to detach. The operation requires `expectedUpdatedAt`, changes only the selected node's parent edge, and rejects stale revisions, self-parenting, cycles, missing parents, and cross-owner placement with structured conflicts. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Upload one image or video to any owned Life Link
post.description: The multipart field name is `file`. One file of at most 25 MiB is accepted, with at most eight media records per Life Link. Supported MIME types are image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, and video/quicktime. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Read media from one owned Life Link
get.description: This canonical route is owner-only, including for public Life Links. Public media remains reachable only through the existing QR-keyed media boundary.

delete.summary: Delete media from one owned Life Link
delete.description: Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: List projects owned by the authenticated user

post.summary: Create a project for the authenticated user
post.description: Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Create and persist a batch of unclaimed QR links
post.description: Supported callers send an integer count from 1 through 10000. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Download a batch mapping as CSV
Download a batch mapping and SVG QR images as ZIP
Resolve the viewer-filtered state of a QR link
get.description: Authentication is optional. Owners receive their private content; unauthenticated or non-owner viewers receive the public, private-placeholder, unclaimed, or not-found state allowed by the canonical store policy. Non-owner claimed responses force ownerId and compatibility projectId to null, force any projected media ownerId to null, and never expose canonical Life Link identity, parent, ancestry, children, path, root, descendant, or hierarchy fields.

post.summary: Idempotently claim a QR or attach it to an eligible owned Life Link
post.description: `commandId` in the JSON body and `Idempotency-Key` in the header are two bindings for the same command identity; when both are present, the non-empty body value takes precedence. Replaying the same command identity for the same effective owner and QR returns the recorded claim result with the current authorized QR state. Reusing it for a different owner or QR returns `idempotency_key_conflict`. Create-and-bind remains the default when `mode` is omitted; explicit `mode: attach` requires `lifeLinkId` and binds only an eligible existing untagged Life Link owned by the caller. Replay/conflict comparison also binds the mode and requested target. If neither command binding is supplied, the server generates an identity. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Compare a scanned QR value with a target QR identifier
post.description: The scan value may be a Life Links QR URL or a bare Life Links QR identifier. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Open the stable browser page for a QR link
get.description: Returns the Life Links browser application shell. The browser application resolves viewer-filtered QR state through `GET /api/qr/{qrId}`.

BearerSession.description: Opaque native session token returned only by login with `client: native`.

XRequestId.name: X-Request-Id
XRequestId.description: Optional caller-supplied request correlation identifier. A valid value is echoed in the response. A missing value, a value outside the accepted grammar, or a value in the native session-token lexical space is ignored and replaced with a server-generated UUID.

LifeLinkId.name: lifeLinkId
LifeLinkId.description: Stable canonical Life Link identity, independent of QR identity.

ParentLifeLinkId.name: parentId
ParentLifeLinkId.description: Owned parent whose immediate children should be listed. Omit to list top-level Life Links.

LifeLinkCursor.name: cursor
LifeLinkCursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor returned by the same operation and sort context. Callers must not construct or interpret it.

LifeLinkPageLimit.name: limit
LifeLinkPageLimit.description: Maximum number of immediate children or search results. The default is 25; accepted values are integers from 1 through 100.

LifeLinkSearchQuery.name: q
LifeLinkSearchQuery.description: Owner-scoped title, body, recorded-path, or QR search text.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional claim or attach command identity. The non-empty JSON `commandId` takes precedence when both bindings are supplied.

BrowserOrigin.name: Origin
BrowserOrigin.description: Required by deployment policy for browser mutations unless a same-origin Referer is available. Authenticated native bearer calls, and native login requests, may omit browser-origin headers.

RequestId.description: Request correlation identifier accepted from a valid X-Request-Id request header or generated by the server. Values in the service's native session-token lexical space are rejected and replaced with a generated identifier so credentials cannot enter logs through this header.

RetryAfter.description: Whole seconds until the active rate-limit bucket resets.

SessionCookie.description: Browser session cookie. Login sets it only when `client: native` is absent; logout clears it.

ContentDisposition.description: Inline media filename or attachment download filename.

CacheControl.description: Owner media uses `private, no-store`; public media uses `public, max-age=300`.

LifeLinkId.description: Stable canonical Life Link identity. It is not a QR identifier and remains stable when a QR is attached.

LifeLinkCursor.description: Opaque bounded continuation token scoped to one list or search ordering.

ownerId.description: Owner identity for owner-authorized responses; null in non-owner public QR projections.
Owner identity for an authorized owner projection; null in a non-owner public claimed projection.

projectId.description: Compatibility Project placement for an authorized owner projection; null in a non-owner public claimed projection.

qrId.description: The one QR currently bound to this Life Link, or null. QR identity never replaces Life Link identity.

updatedAt.description: Canonical optimistic-concurrency revision supplied as expectedUpdatedAt for content and parent mutations.

bodyDoc.description: Optional structured document coordinated with body. Serialized JSON is limited to 128 KiB and normalized to at most 16 levels.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Exact updatedAt revision from the Life Link being edited.

bodyDoc.description: The serialized JSON document is limited to 128 KiB and nesting is normalized to at most 16 levels.

parentId.description: Replacement parent identity, or null to detach this Life Link to the top level.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Exact updatedAt revision from the Life Link being moved.

client.description: When present, selects the native bearer-token response instead of the browser cookie response.

sessionToken.description: Returned only for native login. Store as an opaque bearer credential.

bodyDoc.description: The serialized JSON document is limited to 128 KiB and nesting is normalized to at most 16 levels.

oneOf.description: Default create-and-bind mode. `mode` may be omitted for all existing clients.
Attach mode binds the QR to one eligible existing untagged Life Link owned by the caller.

commandId.description: Optional claim or attach command identity. After trimming, a non-empty body value takes precedence over Idempotency-Key; an empty value is treated as absent.

lifeLinkId.description: Required only in attach mode; identifies the eligible existing untagged Life Link.

oneOf.description: Decoded QR path segment or bare Life Links identifier parsed from scanText. URL path segments are reported even when they are not valid canonical Life Links identifiers.

LoginOk.description: Authenticated user and QR base URL. Browser login also sets the session cookie; native login returns sessionToken in the JSON body.

LogoutNoContent.description: Session deleted when present and browser cookie cleared.

MeOk.description: Current user when authenticated, otherwise null.

LinkListOk.description: Links owned by the current user.

LifeLinkListOk.description: Deterministically ordered, bounded page of top-level Life Links or one parent's immediate children.

LifeLinkSearchOk.description: Bounded owner-scoped search results with path context and opaque continuation metadata.

LifeLinkDetailOk.description: Exact owned Life Link with bounded ancestry and immediate-child context.

LifeLinkUpdated.description: Updated or moved canonical Life Link with its new optimistic-concurrency revision.

LifeLinkMediaCreated.description: Created canonical Life Link media metadata.

LifeLinkMediaContent.description: Owner-authorized canonical Life Link media bytes. This route always uses private, no-store caching.

MediaContent.description: Media bytes. Private media is disclosed only to its owner; denied private reads use the same 404 response as missing media.

ProjectListOk.description: Projects owned by the current user.

QrBatchCreated.description: Persisted QR batch and its unclaimed QR links.

QrBatchZip.description: ZIP attachment containing mapping.csv and SVG QR images.

QrStateOk.description: Viewer-filtered unclaimed, private-placeholder, or claimed QR state.

QrNotFound.description: The QR identifier does not exist. Unlike generic route errors, this is a typed QR state response.

ClaimOk.description: The QR was created-and-bound, attached to the requested eligible Life Link, or was already owned by this caller. Same-command replay returns the recorded result with the current authorized QR state.

ClaimNotFound.description: The QR identifier does not exist, or an attach target is not visible to the authenticated owner.

ClaimConflict.description: The QR belongs to another owner, the supplied command identity is already bound to a different effective owner, QR, mode, or requested target, or attach eligibility failed.

FindScanOk.description: Parsed scan identifier and exact target match result.

BrowserPageOk.description: Life Links browser application HTML shell.

NoContent.description: The mutation completed and returns no body.

LifeLinkBadRequest.description: The canonical Life Link request, cursor, structured body, or output bound is invalid.

LifeLinkNotFound.description: The canonical Life Link or requested canonical media was missing or deliberately hidden because the caller is not its owner.

LifeLinkConflict.description: The canonical operation conflicts with current revision, hierarchy, QR-binding, or stable-identity state. Expected failures use a bounded stable code and optional reason.

BadRequest.description: The request failed input or multipart validation.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication failed, or a valid Life Links session is required.

Forbidden.description: The browser Origin or same-origin Referer did not satisfy the configured mutation-origin policy.

NotFound.description: The resource was missing or deliberately hidden because the caller is not its owner.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The uploaded media file exceeded 25 MiB.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The uploaded media MIME type is outside the supported image and video set.

RateLimited.description: The active request bucket is rate limited.
